note: Judged 2026-10-12 by an independent judge (authored none of 9114a04414, 27be2c4a3c) against rfc/full/rfc4090.txt Section 6.4.3: "When the PLR detects a link or/and node failure condition, it has to reroute the data traffic onto the bypass tunnel and to start sending the control traffic for the protected LSP onto the bypass tunnel." Row text is a verbatim span of that sentence. Producer read: frr.go::repairedPathSelection (exact compare of PSB.ReceivedERO, set on every transit acceptance in engine.go::handlePathTransit, with remainingERO of the refresh), engine.go::handlePath (a repaired selection skips resolveReceivedPath) and handlePathTransit (repaired -> sendPath, which takes the bypass). Positive TestRepairedLSPKeepsUpstreamRefresh: after the link-down repair and native routing moved off the failed link, an ingress PATH refresh naming the accepted route draws no PathErr, is relayed exactly once with the bypass's TableID and the PLR's sender, the repair stays in use, and the MP's RESV for the PLR sender is accepted with the [5000 24000] stack. It goes red if control traffic is refused, dropped, or sent off the bypass. Negative TestRepairedLSPChangedEROResolvedAgain: a refresh whose ERO no longer passes the merge point (first downstream hop dropped, or another strict hop) is not relayed on the bypass and is resolved again to PathErr 24/2. That is a violation of this row, not only a neighbour: the bypass ends at the MP and Section 6.4.4 builds the backup ERO from the first address belonging to the MP, so a route that no longer names the MP is not the protected LSP's control traffic. Case 1 also discriminates the replaced one-hop length heuristic. Both records are mutants on frr.go line 700 (true/false) from a hand-written one-mutant report whose file, line and original text match HEAD; the recorder applies the break by overlay and refuses an unobserved red, and the logic predicts both reds (true: refusal reddens the positive's NotEqual PathErr; false: case 1 relays a PATH). Scope note: the immediate backup PATH at repair (tryLocalRepair's sendPath) is not observed by these units, which count only after the repair; it is asserted by the RFC4090-6.4-1/6.4-2 units in rfc4090_frr_bypass_test.go and by TestSelectedBypassCarriesAllProtectedControl, and with it removed control traffic still reaches the bypass at the next refresh. The RFC's "has to" carries the [MUST] class row RFC4090-6.4.3-1 already uses.
